candidates.original_title: Interruptibility of software developers and its prediction using psycho-physiological sensors
candidates.description: The original lab study claimed that biometric sensors can predict the interruptibility of software developers with high accuracy (91.5%) in a controlled lab environment.
candidates.citation_sentence: In this paper, we report on what is, to the best of our knowledge, the first external and close replication of the original lab study (Züger and Fritz 2015).
candidates.notes: The paper explicitly states it is an external close replication of the original lab study. The replication failed to replicate the original's high-accuracy classification results; models did not significantly outperform the majority classifier baseline. AQ5 was not replicated due to an incorrect post-interview questionnaire (noted in Section 6.4). The authors explicitly state they cannot replicate models that significantly improve over the majority classifier baseline. Severe threats to validity were identified: small sample size (10 participants), highly imbalanced dataset, and ad hoc transformation of the interruptibility scale. EDA features were dropped after sessions due to a measurement error (electrode saturation), which may have affected model performance.

candidates.original_title: Interruptibility of software developers and its prediction using psycho-physiological sensors
candidates.description: Shorter time windows, particularly a 10-second window, produce better interruptibility-classification performance than longer time windows.
candidates.citation_sentence: In this paper, we report on what is, to the best of our knowledge, the first external and close replication of the original lab study (Züger and Fritz 2015).
candidates.notes: The replication found no consistent advantage for shorter or longer time windows, unlike the original study.

candidates.original_title: Interruptibility of software developers and its prediction using psycho-physiological sensors
candidates.description: Biometric sensor data can predict software developers' perceived interruptibility with high accuracy, significantly outperforming a majority-classifier baseline in a controlled laboratory setting.
candidates.citation_sentence: In this paper, we report on what is, to the best of our knowledge, the first external and close replication of the original lab study (Züger and Fritz 2015).
candidates.notes: The authors explicitly state that they could not replicate models that significantly improve over the majority-classifier baseline and conclude that the original results did not generalize. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Interruptibility of software developers and its prediction using psycho-physiological sensors
candidates.description: Perceived mental workload is strongly negatively associated with software developers' perceived interruptibility.
candidates.citation_sentence: In this paper, we report on what is, to the best of our knowledge, the first external and close replication of the original lab study (Züger and Fritz 2015).
candidates.notes: The replication found a statistically significant association in the expected direction, but it was substantially weaker than in the original study. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Interruptibility of software developers and its prediction using psycho-physiological sensors
candidates.description: Interruptions are more disruptive to software developers during periods of high mental workload.
candidates.citation_sentence: In this paper, we report on what is, to the best of our knowledge, the first external and close replication of the original lab study (Züger and Fritz 2015).
candidates.notes: The replication did not observe a statistically significant association between perceived interruptibility and disruptiveness. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Interruptibility of software developers and its prediction using psycho-physiological sensors
candidates.description: Interruption lag is weakly associated with software developers' perceived interruptibility.
candidates.citation_sentence: In this paper, we report on what is, to the best of our knowledge, the first external and close replication of the original lab study (Züger and Fritz 2015).
candidates.notes: Both the original and replication reported a weak, statistically significant association between interruption lag and perceived interruptibility. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
